cues.text: Let go by Arsenal
Harry Kane was born in London in 1993.
He started playing for a local club, Ridgeway Rovers, when he was six.
At eight, he joined the youth academy of Arsenal.
But after one season, they let him go.
The man in charge later said they felt Harry was not very athletic.
Turn the signpost.
Harry also had a trial at Tottenham Hotspur, but at first it did not work out.
So he went back to his old club, Ridgeway Rovers, and kept playing.
Being let go hurts. Going back to people who know you can help you grow again.
Not the biggest, not the fastest
In 2004, when Harry was eleven, he went on trial at Watford.
He played well for Watford against Tottenham, and Tottenham gave him another chance.
At first, Harry did not stand out.
He was not big, and not very quick.
Born in July, he was younger than many boys in his school year.
Pull the tab.
But his coaches noticed how much he always wanted to improve.
A couple of years later, he had a big growth spurt that made him taller and stronger.
Everyone grows at their own speed. Keep practising while you wait for your time.
Sent away to learn
Harry signed his first professional contract with Tottenham in 2010.
His coach, Tim Sherwood, thought he could learn by playing for other clubs first.
So in 2011 he went on loan to Leyton Orient, and then to Millwall.
Follow the suitcase.
At Millwall, Harry took time to get going.
Then he scored seven goals in his last fourteen games, and he was named Millwall’s Young Player of the Year.
Starting again at a new club is hard, but he kept going.
Being sent somewhere new can feel like a step back. It can also help you learn.
A broken foot
In 2012, Harry went on loan to Norwich City.
In only his second game there, he broke a bone in his foot.
He had to stop playing and spend months getting better back at Tottenham.
Flip the calendar.
Harry worked to recover and returned to play.
Soon he moved on loan again, to Leicester City.
He scored on his home debut, but he often started on the bench, and Leicester were knocked out of the play-offs.
Getting better after an injury takes patience. Small steps each day add up.
Ready for his chance
In April 2014, Harry finally started a Premier League game for Tottenham, and he scored.
The next season, the new manager, Mauricio Pochettino, picked him again and again.
Harry scored 21 league goals.
Flip the team sheet.
There were hard moments too.
When Tottenham lost the League Cup final, Harry called it the worst feeling in the world.
But he was named the PFA Young Player of the Year, and in 2015 he scored on his England debut.
Keep working, even while you wait. Then you’ll be ready when your chance comes.
After the missed penalty
Harry became England’s captain, and in 2018 he was the top scorer at the World Cup.
But at the 2022 World Cup, in the quarter-final against France, he missed a penalty, and England lost 2–1.
Many people would feel very sad after a moment like that.
Take the next penalty.
A few months later, in 2023, Harry stepped up to take a penalty against Italy, and he scored.
It was his 54th goal for England, making him the country’s all-time top scorer.
You are more than one miss. Be brave and try again.
